<answer>
**Confirmed finding — simulation loading indicator is rendered after computation, so it does not provide feedback while the work runs.** In `/home/rafael/Projetos/App/pages/2_Simulação.py:435-445`, the page writes “Rodando simulações…” before the calls, but Streamlit sends the completed page after the script run; the actual simulation and bootstrap calls are at lines 532-538, and the indicator is removed at line 855. During a slow run, users therefore wait without seeing that status. Smallest fix: use the existing `loading_overlay()` context manager around the simulation and bootstrap work, keeping its live status semantics and flat shared styling. Acceptance check: trigger a deliberately slow simulation and verify the status is visible before completion and disappears once results render.

**No other concrete UX or visual issue evidenced.** The portfolio flow has explicit selection/restore notices and actionable empty states (`pages/1_Portfolio.py:528-546`), delays price retrieval until “Carregar portfólio” (`:633-641`), reports quote/history errors (`:675-731`), and links completed analysis to Simulation (`:1936-1941`). Simulation guards stale or missing portfolio state with an actionable link (`pages/2_Simulação.py:233-270`), and its form, results, and chart labels are covered by page tests. Shared CSS includes responsive breakpoints, visible focus treatment, and reduced-motion support (`style.css:1155-1162`, `:1215-1222`, `:2310-2326`). No additional confirmed problem met the requested evidence threshold.
</answer>
